text: The quality-triage.json uses a 'files' dict (not a flat 'candidates' list) for per-file decisions — the top-level candidates field is null; all individual keep/drop decisions are inside triage.files[filename].candidates. The top-level 'groups' array documents group-drop patterns only.

In the Nova quality batch, TRY002 (ruff raise-vanilla-class) and W0719 (pylint broad-exception-raised) fire on the same `raise Exception(...)` lines — all 37 TRY002 candidates are co-located duplicates of W0719 candidates; drop TRY002 as duplicates and retain W0719 at medium severity.

Lizard nesting-metric findings for a nested function produce overlapping lineRanges with the enclosing function's nesting finding (the inner range is fully contained in the outer). The integrity rule prohibits overlapping same-rule findings; keep only the innermost range per nested-function pair.

When verifying a trim-to-25-findings fix, check both that no high-severity findings were wrongly excluded AND that the final array is sorted high→medium→low; a line-number-ordered trim can produce correct content but wrong presentation order.

When verifying a sort-only ordering fix on capped findings files, only the JSON array ordering and finding count need checking — the candidate selection (which 25 are kept) does not change and does not need re-verification.
